newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Interest rate fears rattles dlr, euro stocks.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Interest rate fears rattles dlr, euro stocks.

text.p: Interest rate uncertainty dominated financial markets on Tuesday, sending the dollar on a roller-coaster ride and causing sharp drops in European stocks.

The dollar bounced back by nearly two yen from five-month lows and stood above 113 yen in early afternoon trade after Japanese officials warned the yen's rise had been too rapid and a Japanese rate rise was not likely soon.
Currency markets had earlier sold dollars because of worries that Japan might increase rates, making dollar-denominated assets less attractive to investors.

In sharp contrast, European bourses fell steeply because of fears that U.S. interest rates could be increased by U.S. central bank FOMC policy-makers when they meet this afternoon. Their decision is not expected until 1815 GMT.
"The dollar has recovered after Sakakibara (Eisuke) said the yen's rise had been too rapid," said Alessandra Stagliano, economist at Daiwa Europe.

Sakakibara, director-general of the Finance Ministry's International Finance Bureau, and known as "Mr Yen" for his influence over markets, said the pace of the yen's strengthening against the dollar was too rapid and that volatility was undesirable.
Sakakibara, speaking to Reuters, said too much volatility in foreign exchange markets was undesirable and that Japan would "deal appropriately" with such excessive volatility.

The dollar fell by nearly four yen overnight in Asia after reports that a committee of Japan's ruling Liberal Democratic Partly (LDP) was considering asking for higher discount rates from the Bank of Japan.
Despite the reassurances from Tokyo, the dollar remained well below the levels seen in late Europe on Monday.
Currency traders -- unlike their equity colleagues-- detected a shift of mood in Washington's commitment to a strong dollar before the meeting of the FOMC (Federal Open Market Committee).

They cited comments by Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin as evidence of Washington's change in tune. Rubin said the U.S. policy on the dollar remained unchanged -- but did not explicitly repeat his past support for a strong dollar.
The dollar, which clawed back early losses to reach 113.45 yen, has been spiralling downward since hitting a 56-month peak of 127.47 on May 1. Against the mark, it was down nearly two pfennigs.

"Rubin's accumulated comments, the possibility the LDP will push for higher rates and the absence of any comments by the Japanese to halt the move...all helped the move," said Tim Fox, treasury economist at Standard Chartered.
The uncertainty over U.S. rates went the other way in European bourses where the fear was that rates would go up and this cast a cloud over markets. A poor start in Wall Street added to the gloom.
London, Frankfurt and Paris all fell by over one percent as investors counted the potential rise in the cost of doing business.
Frankfurt suffered the most, with floor trade ending down 1.7 percent as the weaker dollar also hit exporting sectors. Many investors took up defensive positions before the FOMC.

Paris fared little better. The blue-chip CAC-40 index was down 1.6 percent in early afternoon trade with the market divided over whether there would be no-change or a quarter percentage point rise in U.S. interest rates.

"We're coming up to a couple of key events -- the FOMC meeting, the French (parliamentary) election -- and the market's at record highs. It's normal to correct," one trader said. The CAC index rose 5.71 percent last week.
London fell about one percent in thin trade with many investors sitting on the fence awaiting the FOMC's decision.
"The market looks set to continue drifting off," said one dealer. "But there's no real selling pressure, its just nerves ahead of the FOMC."
STOCK PRICES AT 1430 GMT
London's FTSE 100 was down 43.0 points at 4,602.2.
The Paris CAC-40 index was down 44.33 points at 2,739.95.
Frankfurt's DAX index closed down 61.12 points at 3,543.43.
CURRENCIES AT 1430 GMT
The dollar stood at 1.6949 marks and 113.45 yen compared with 1.7105 marks and 116.09 yen in late European trade on Monday.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed in the afternooj at $343.00 an ounce, compared with Monday's close in London of $341.25. Silver was at $4.72, up three cents.
